title: Interpreting the Feedback to 'Take a Step Up'
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This piece unpacks a common but vague piece of leadership feedback — telling a high performer to 'take a step up' — and translates it into concrete behaviors. Citing Bill Walsh's line that champions behave like champions before they're champions, the article explains that taking a step up means acting with the confidence, ownership, and initiative of the next role before being formally promoted into it: advocating more persuasively, taking on unclaimed problems, being more candid, and identifying risks and opportunities proactively. It reframes the vague phrase as, at its core, a compliment and an expression of belief in the person's potential, even though leaders rarely explain what they mean when they say it.
points: The instruction to 'take a step up' is usually left vague, which leaves the recipient confused or even offended.
Bill Walsh's line — champions behave like champions before they are champions — captures the real ask.
Concretely, it means advocating more persuasively, owning problems, and being more candid before formal promotion.
It also includes proactively identifying risks and pursuing new opportunities for the team.
Despite the vagueness, the feedback is meant as a compliment reflecting belief in someone's potential.
quotes: The vision they have in their minds is of a team member with the initiative to take on the responsibilities of even more leadership.
In the words of legendary NFL coach Bill Walsh, “Champions behave like champions before they are champions.

Take up more space, advocate more persuasively for your ideas, insist on being involved in critical decisions, hold others accountable, and possess the confidence to be even more candid in your feedback to others, including your leader.
As someone who is being asked to take on more leadership responsibility, the leader also wants you to own all problems on the team and to take the initiative to resolve or manage them.
Leaders who offer this feedback do so because they believe the team member is ready for the challenge.
